chunks: Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
And he recited this Verse: 'This was because they disbelieved in the Signs of Allah and killed the Prophets unjustly; this was because they disobeyed and exceeded the limits.'

He said: 'By Allah, they did not kill them by their hands, nor did they strike them with their swords, but they heard their narrations, publicized them, so they were seized upon it and killed. Thus, it became murder, transgression, and disobedience.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Israelites kill the prophets according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanism of 'killing' prophets by elucidating that the Israelites' primary act was publicizing the prophets' teachings to the masses, which led to their execution. This interpretation highlights how the dissemination of divine truth, when met with rejection, transformed into a capital offense, thereby constituting the 'transgression' (i'tida') and 'disobedience' (ma'siyah) cited in the Quranic verse. This scholarly insight underscores the political and social dynamics of early Islamic history, where the 'publicizing' of the message was often the precursor to persecution.

en.hubeali: Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws and recited this Verse [2:61] this was so because they disbelieved in the Signs of Allah and killed the Prophets unjustly; this was so because they disobeyed and exceeded the limits.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They did not kill them<sup>as</sup> by their hands nor did they strike them<sup>as</sup> by their swords, but they heard their<sup>as</sup> Ahadeeth, for they publicised these, so they<sup>as</sup> were seized upon it and they were killed. Thus, it came to be murder, and transgression, and a disobedience’.
en.sarwar: 6. Yunus has narrated from ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following: “The Imam recited this verse: . . for they denied the evidence (of the existence of Allah) and murdered His Prophets without reason; they were disobedient transgressors.’ [2:61]

The Imam said, ‘By Allah they did not murder them with their hands or swords but they would hear their Hadith and publicize them, causing them to be captured and murdered. It then became murder, transgression and disobedience.’”
